results.title: Everyone in the AI build is selling the same option to a different buyer
highlights:
Nebius, which raised its price while the market fell.

On 17 September, Nebius told customers that selected pay-as-you-go GPU rates rise 17% to 21% on 1 October. H100 goes from $3.85 to $4.50 an hour, H200 from $4.50 to $5.40, B200 from $7.15 to $8.50 and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50. By the 19th, the executed market went the other way. H100 was $2.85 versus $3.02 the day before and H200 was $5.13 versus $5.60. The new H100 card is 57.9% above the latest executed price.

I do not think that makes the list price useless though. Nebius still publishes preemptible rates of $2.15 for H100 and $2.45 for H200, and says a large multi-month reservation can get up to 35% off. Same accelerator, three prices. The fully flexible one is the one getting more expensive. You pay more if you want to turn up whenever you like.

Sources: Nebius pricing page and customer notice via Reuters, Ornn cross-GPU settlements. B300 is excluded because there is no executed settlement for it.

So the real product is the spread, not the price.

If the preemptible rates stay where they are, the on-demand premium on H100 goes from $1.70 to $2.35 an hour. B300 goes from $3.55 to $5.20. Nebius has not published future preemptible rates, so I am holding those flat for now. The price increase lands on the customer who refuses to commit.

Sources: Nebius pricing page and the announced 1 October on-demand reset. The second series assumes preemptible rates hold.

Take the full 35% commitment discount off the new H100 card and you get $2.93, basically where the executed market was. Nebius can raise the public on-demand price and still sign a committed customer around the old effective level. Its $775m secured facility is underwritten against GPU infrastructure and contracted cash flows at SOFR plus 250. An hourly customer turning into a committed one helps the financing even if the effective GPU-hour price barely moves.

results.title: Nebius hikes AI cloud prices again as demand | UXC News
highlights:
Nebius announced a second price hike for Nvidia GPU and other compute instances, reflecting the rapid surge in AI training and inference demand.

Nebius, the Russian cloud‑computing arm of Sberbank, announced a second increase in prices for its Nvidia GPU‑powered and other high‑performance compute instances, citing a “rapid surge” in demand for artificial‑intelligence training and inference workloads.

## Why the price hike matters

The new rates, which apply to both on‑demand and reserved instances, push Nebius’s pricing above that of many Western providers, raising concerns for startups and research labs that rely on affordable access to large‑scale GPU clusters.

Nebius officials said the adjustment reflects “the unprecedented growth in AI workloads across the region,” and is intended to sustain the company’s ability to expand its hardware inventory and maintain service reliability.

### Scope of the increase

The hike targets Nvidia A100 and H100 GPU instances, as well as CPU‑only compute nodes used for data preprocessing and model serving. Nebius did not disclose the exact percentage change, but industry observers estimate a rise of roughly 10‑15 % compared with the previous pricing tier introduced six months ago.

results.title: B200 on-demand costs $6.03 an hour. H100 FP8 spot costs $0.99, a fraction of that price. On sticker price alone, H100 looks like the deal. It still does once you account for … | Spheron Network
highlights:
# B200 on-demand costs $6.03 an hour. H100 FP8 spot costs $0.99, a fraction of that price. On sticker price alone, H100 looks like the deal. It still does once you account for … | Spheron Network · LinkedIn · 2026-09-20T00:00:00+00:00

**Spheron Network**.

---

B200 on-demand costs $6.03 an hour. H100 FP8 spot costs $0.99, a fraction of that price. On sticker price alone, H100 looks like the deal. It still does once you account for throughput.

The hourly rate ignores how much work each GPU finishes in that hour. FP8 and FP4 are number formats a GPU computes in. FP4 uses fewer bits per number than FP8, so it moves less data and processes more tokens per second.

MLPerf is an independent benchmark, not a Spheron-run test, and its numbers are the best available proxy for real throughput. On MLPerf v4.1, H100 FP8 spot produces 24,525 tokens per second. On MLPerf v5.1, B200 FP4 produces 102,725, about 4.2 times more.

Normalize price for that throughput gap and the ranking holds:

- H100 FP8 spot: about $0.090 per million tokens
- B200 FP4, on-demand: about $0.130 per million tokens

H100 still costs less per million tokens, even running at a fraction of B200 FP4's throughput. These figures come from Spheron's own FP4 quantization benchmark post and may shift as pricing and benchmarks update.

results.title: RunPod price change — RunPod raises Secure Cloud GPU rates; Commu | UsagePricing
highlights:
Price change September 20, 2026

# RunPod raises Secure Cloud GPU rates; Community Cloud held flat

Secure Cloud Pods: B300 $7.39/hr, B200 $5.89/hr, H200 $4.39/hr, H100 SXM $2.99/hr, A100 PCIe $1.39/hr, A100 SXM $1.49/hr, RTX 4090 $0.69/hr Secure Cloud Pods: B300 $7.89/hr, B200 $6.79/hr, H200 $4.59/hr, H100 SXM $3.49/hr, A100 PCIe and A100 SXM $1.59/hr, RTX 4090 $0.74/hr

This is the first broad rise across RunPod’s Secure Cloud Pod card since we began tracking it, and it lands hardest on the data-center GPUs: H100 SXM is up 17%, B200 15% and A100 PCIe 14%. Eight rates held, including H100 PCIe and H100 NVL. The pricing page is stamped “Updated September 13, 2026”, so the new rates may have been live for up to a week before we recorded them.

What it means for buyers. Community Cloud rates did not move, so the gap between the two clouds widened. B200 used to cost more on Community Cloud ($5.98/hr) than on Secure Cloud ($5.89/hr); it is now $0.81/hr cheaper there. If your workload does not need Secure Cloud, Community Cloud is now the cheaper option for every GPU on the card. If it does, budget about 17% more for H100 SXM hours.

...

RunPod runs a dual-cloud GPU marketplace: Secure Cloud (enterprise-grade DCs, redundant infrastructure) and Community Cloud (partner DCs, lower cost with reduced reliability). Secure Cloud per-hour Pods: RTX 4090 $0.89, A40 $0.59, A100 PCIe $1.79, A100 SXM $1.79, H100 PCIe $2.89, H100 NVL $3.19, H100 SXM $3.99, H200 $5.29, B200 $7.99, B300 (288GB HBM3e) $8.99. RunPod raised Secure Cloud rates twice in about a month: a September 2026 reprice lifted 11 rates, and an October 2026 reprice (page stamped "Updated October 8, 2026") lifted 15 of 21 by another 11 to 20 percent, reaching the low end of the card as well as the frontier. Since mid-July 2026, H100 SXM has gone from $2.99 to $3.99 per hour and B200 from $5.89 to $7.99. Every Community Cloud rate held through both moves, so Community Cloud is now cheaper than Secure Cloud on all 21 GPU types, by 16 percent to 62 percent. RunPod published no notice period, no grandfathering and no rate-change log for either increase, and the only self-serve rate lock is a Savings plan that RunPod has since deprecated for new purchases.
